grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, milk, natural yoghurt, sultanas, pears, hazelnuts and honey are all plain home-kitchen foods with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every item is an everyday Tesco purchase, and 50g of hazelnuts is not a treat-level spend.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, a grater and a small frying pan, with simple stirring, grating and toasting.

works.reason: 200g oats soaked in 400ml milk and 150g yoghurt, with three pears, makes a well-balanced bircher for four, and an overnight soak softens the oats properly.

honest_times.reason: Twelve minutes covers stirring, grating, toasting, chopping and slicing; the 480 minutes is the unattended overnight soak noted in the time note, and the morning work stays quick.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the cinnamon and the lemon squeeze, is used in the steps, sultanas match the raisins id, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Pears are at their best in early October and form the core of the dish, both grated through the oats and sliced on top.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English that a beginner could follow, with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling breakfast of oats, dairy, fruit and nuts, with only a modest drizzle of honey.
